metadata.description: Per-environment flash and RAM build-size budgets for protoArtoo firmware
notes: Flash: binary image size (.bin file) to fit in the OTA partition (from partitions/*.csv app0/app1 size field)
RAM: static allocation (.data + .bss sections from linker via size -A), not heap or PSRAM

dram_limit_bytes: length of the linker's static-DRAM segment (dram0_0_seg in the generated memory.ld) under the platform's current configuration - informational only, no tool reads it. artoo-esp32=180736B now that Bluetooth is compiled out (it read 124580B while the BT controller reserved its window); esp32-p4=327680B
Budgets set with deliberate headroom to prevent reflexive raises on legitimate commits
Env-to-platform classification in 'platforms' registry; Makefile/slice_verify.py/check_build_budgets.py all consume it

platforms.esp32p4.envs must list EVERY platformio.ini env whose resolved platform is the P4 one (test_build_budgets.py checks this against platformio.ini): a P4 env missing here builds in the artoo-esp32 core dir and swaps that Arduino core in place. Only envs with an entry under 'envs' below are size-checked

Baseline measurements recorded with commit SHA (git cat-file -t to verify); baseline_* fields are informational only - check_build_budgets.py and slice_verify.py enforce flash_budget_bytes, flash_ceiling_bytes and ram_budget_bytes, never the baselines

Baseline method: flash = .pio/build/<env>/firmware.bin size; RAM = .data + .bss from the platform size tool (-A) on firmware.elf, i.e. slice_verify.get_build_sizes(); measured on a clean tree at the recorded commit (no -dirty stamp)

artoo_esp32.budget_rationale: Measured 1,391,856 B flash (87.0% of the budget, 81.7% of the partition) and 100,900 B static RAM at baseline_measured_at, where the Framework Envelope in platformio.ini compiles out the framework facilities this controller does not offer. Against the 1,596,112 B / 102,600 B image built from the same packages at the parent commit that is -204,256 B flash and -1,700 B RAM. Hard ceiling at 1,671,936 B (partition 1,703,936 - 32,000 B reserve for OTA headers/metadata). Flash budget stays at 1,600,000 B: the recovered bytes are headroom for in-flight work, not a new floor. The RAM budget (110,000 B until the raise recorded at the end of this note) is a heap-headroom figure, not a percentage of dram_limit_bytes - static .data+.bss shares the DRAM segment with the heap, and the request-admission floors in include/web_admission.h are calibrated against the largest free block, so a static byte saved is a heap byte gained. Compiling out Bluetooth widened the linker's static-DRAM segment from 124,580 to 180,736 B, but that is not room gained: static data now starts at 0x3FFB0000, inside the window the Bluetooth controller used to reserve and the firmware used to release to the heap at boot, and the heap starts where static data ends (#381), so every static byte is still a heap byte and the real ceiling this budget guards has not moved. RAM budget raised 110,000 -> 112,000 B on 2026-09-10 (operator decision, epic #175) to carry ONE deliberate spend: the addressed Servo Output row table (#338), 24 rows x up to four Part ids at 13 B each plus the fixed fields, measured at 770 B with a single Part slot and projected at about 1,706 B with four. Sized to that spend and no rounder: the figure above is heap headroom, so every byte added here is a byte the admission floors in include/web_admission.h no longer have, and the runtime evidence for those floors is g_webRefusedHeapFloor / g_webRefusedHeapFloorDiag on a board rather than anything a build can show. The next raise is owed the same arithmetic.
artoo_esp32.fs_budget_rationale: DERIVED, NOT RATCHETED (#382, 2026-09-13; re-derived for a cap of five by #426, 2026-09-25; re-derived for one take by #442, 2026-10-03). The filesystem partition holds three things that compete for the same 160 blocks: this web image, the builder's Learned Sequences and the builder's one take, both of which the firmware writes to /seq at runtime. So the budget is what the partition can give the image while everything the firmware promises still fits: 160 blocks, minus four full sequences, minus one full take, minus the free space the last save demands. The artoo-esp32 stores five sequences (SEQ_STORE_CAP, include/seq_store_util.h; operator decision 2026-09-25, ADR 0065 amendment) and one take (TAKE_STORE_CAP, include/take_store_util.h; operator decision 2026-09-30 on #442, ADR 0061 correction), and either file is at most 12 KB here (PA_SEQ_FILE_MAX_KB; TAKE_FILE_MAX_BYTES is the same figure); a save of either is refused unless free >= 2 x 12 KB + the file (src/seq_store_util.cpp, src/take_store.cpp), so the last save needs 36,864 B = 9 free blocks. Free, to the firmware, is total minus LittleFS.usedBytes(), and usedBytes() is block_size x lfs_fs_size() (esp_littlefs.c get_total_and_used_bytes), which counts BOTH blocks of every metadata pair; the figure this budget is checked against (tools/check_build_budgets.py) counts only the blocks that have been written. Measured by writing into the real image with the platform's own littlefs-python parameters (block 4096, read/prog 1, cache 4096, lookahead 32, block_cycles 500, name_max 64, disk 2.1, a 4-byte mtime attribute per entry): /seq plus four full 12,288 B files cost 17 written blocks (4 per file, not 3: littlefs adds CTZ skip-list pointers that push a three-block file into a fourth, plus 1 for the directory), a full take costs 4 more - it is a file in /seq like a sequence, never a directory of its own, which would cost a written block and a metadata pair more - and once /seq exists lfs_fs_size() reports 2 more than the written count (the unwritten halves of the root and /seq metadata pairs). 160 - 17 - 4 - 2 - 9 = 128 whole blocks = 524,288 B. Checked by replaying the save paths (a sequence: write /seq/.tmp.json, rename; a take: write /seq/.tmp.take, rename to <owner>.<take>.new, rename to .take when its sequence is saved) under the save rule against the image padded to exactly N written blocks, in every order: at 128, four sequences then the take then the fifth, the take then five, and five then the take are all accepted; at 129 the last save is refused in each of those orders. The same replay reproduces the five-sequence figure this replaces (no take: five accepted at 132, the fifth refused at 133). MEASURED at 39a18736, the take slice's last data/ change: 122 written blocks (499,712 B), 6 blocks under the budget. The replay before that corrected #382's figure: 160 - 37 - 9 = 114 left out the 2 pair-half blocks, and at 114 the tenth save was refused (ten fitted only up to 112). The written count of one staged image depends on the order its files are written: tools/littlefs_image.py now writes largest first on every host (#461); before it, the same 64 staged files at 1ac082d0 imaged as 112 blocks in one worktree and 114 in another. A test holds every filesystem figure here to whole 4,096 B blocks, because 470,016 B (the budget before #382) was 114.75 blocks and its rationale called it 115. The image above this ceiling is not an image that is too big to flash, it is an image that takes the builder's storage: the last of five sequences and a take would be refused before the caps refuse anything. THE BASELINE: 315,392 B in 77 blocks at fs_baseline_measured_at, imaged with -t buildfs (46 staged files, 224,317 B of content), from 113 blocks at b2467053. Two changes bought the 36 blocks: shell delegates no longer inline the Page Recovery View kernel (11 copies, 113 -> 103 priced; ADR 0048 amendment) and tools/gzip_fsdata.py minifies JS and CSS with esbuild before gzipping (-> 77). An image that trips this budget is a decision about storage, not a routine raise: raising it means lowering SEQ_STORE_CAP, TAKE_STORE_CAP or the per-file cap with it, and the arithmetic above is redone. The ratchet history this replaces (100 -> 111 -> 114 blocks, 2026-09-12), the ten-sequence derivation (114 blocks, #382) and the five-sequence one (132 blocks, #426) are in this file's git log.

firebeetle2.budget_rationale: Full firmware: compiles all of src/ against P4 toolchain for production deployment. Hard ceiling at 3,113,728 B (partition 3,145,728 - 32,000 B reserve for OTA headers/metadata). RAM budget raised 100,000 -> 112,000 B on 2026-09-13 (#256 reopen): tools/slice_verify.measure_static_ram at baseline_measured_at reads 107,662 B (.dram0/.dram1 .data+.bss), 7,662 B over the old 100,000 B tripwire. That overrun pre-dates every Wave 0 slice (register row 2 on #381); the 61,214 B baseline stamped at 94880ee was a much older image and nothing re-measured this row while the firmware grew, because the slice gate walks artoo_esp32 only. 112,000 B is sized to the measured figure plus 4,338 B of headroom for in-flight work, the same order as the artoo-esp32 110,000 -> 112,000 raise, not rounded to a comfortable 120,000. Task stacks are xTaskCreate heap and do not appear here. Hardware DRAM (dram_limit_bytes 327,680) is nowhere near. The next raise is owed the same arithmetic. Flash budget stays at 2,000,000 B (measured 1,838,688 B, 91.9%). Flash budget raised 2,000,000 -> 2,200,000 B on 2026-10-03 (operator decision, epic #175): measured 1,986,464 B at 549836ad (99.3%), after #444 linked Wire and the IDF I2C master driver into every image (~26 KB, #381 row 53) and #445 slice 2; #442 (perform on the sticks) is firmware-heavy and would trip it. This is a tripwire, not the limit: the hard ceiling is 3,113,728 B, so 2,200,000 B still leaves 913,728 B of partition. The artoo-esp32 budget is unchanged and is the binding flash constraint (32,720 B left at 549836ad).
firebeetle2.fs_budget_rationale: Measured 655,360 B in 160 written 4,096 B blocks at fs_baseline_measured_at: 83 staged files, 512,387 B of content, the default asset set staged with tools/stage_fsdata.py and priced with tools/fs_price.py --order size, the order tools/littlefs_image.py writes the image in. This is the board's own image and not artoo_esp32's: each board carries its own asset set (ADR 0065, data/asset-sets/), and the product photographs are in the default set here and not in the legacy one. The 397,312 B this row carried before was measured at 0b55e00f, when one data/ image was still built for both boards. Ceiling is the whole 10,354,688 B partition. Budget at 1,048,576 B is deliberately loose and guards a different thing from artoo_esp32's: with 9.5 MB spare there is no scarcity here, so this number exists to catch an accident -- a build that images something enormous -- not to ration. At 160 blocks the image is 96 blocks under the 256 the budget allows.
